paragraphs.text: Neurodevelopmental disorder with or without macrocephaly (NEDMAC) is an X-linked disorder caused by de novo or maternally inherited SMARCA1 variants. Mirzaa et al. (2025) described it in 35 individuals from 26 families. Intellectual disability/developmental delay ranged from mild to severe. Other features included delayed or regressive speech, features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), facial dysmorphism and other variable findings. Macrocephaly was highly penetrant in individuals with truncating variants.

paragraphs.text: Mirzaa et al. (2025) studied a 6-generation family with 4 affected individuals who had mild to severe intellectual disability/developmental delay and brain overgrowth. The proband was a 12-year-old boy with occipitofrontal circumference (OFC) of +6 SD and severe intellectual disability without language. He also had ASD, hydrocephalus treated with a shunt and hepatosplenomegaly, and his height and weight were +5 SD. His brother had OFC of +4.3 SD, mild intellectual disability, hydrocephalus and splenomegaly. Two maternal cousins, a 14-year-old girl and an 8-year-old boy, had OFC of +4.9 and +5.5 SD, respectively. Both had mild learning disability, obesity and a normal brain MRI. Their carrier mothers had OFC of +1 and +1.5 SD and no learning disability.

paragraphs.text: Mirzaa et al. (2025) reported 35 affected individuals (26 males and 9 females) from 26 families, aged 2 to 49 years. Common facial features included frontal bossing, a long face, slanted palpebral fissures, a flat nasal root with a short bulbous nose, anteverted nares and a thin upper lip.
